terms.definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation — supplying an LLM with evidence fetched at query time instead of relying only on its trained weights.
A lexical ranking function scoring documents by term frequency and inverse document frequency; strong at exact terms, IDs and rare words.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion — merges several ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank) per item, with no need to calibrate scores across retrievers.
A dense vector representation of text whose geometric closeness approximates semantic similarity.
Similarity measured as the cosine of the angle between two vectors — direction, not magnitude.
A second-pass model (often a cross-encoder) that rescores a small candidate set by reading the query and passage together for higher precision.
Splitting source documents into retrievable units sized to hold one coherent, answerable idea.
Combining lexical (BM25) and dense vector retrieval, then fusing the results to cover both exact and semantic matches.
A store that indexes embeddings for fast approximate-nearest-neighbour search.
Whether an answer's claims are actually supported by the retrieved evidence, rather than invented.
A fluent but unsupported or fabricated model output.
The attention-based neural architecture underlying modern LLMs.
A mechanism that lets each token weight and draw information from other tokens via query/key/value projections.
Cached key and value tensors from earlier tokens so decoding each new token avoids recomputing the whole sequence.
Rotary Positional Embeddings — encodes token position by rotating query/key vectors, extending gracefully to longer contexts.
Updating a model's weights on task data to change its behaviour or output style — distinct from supplying facts at inference time.
Low-Rank Adaptation — trains small added low-rank matrices instead of full weights, cutting fine-tuning cost.
LoRA applied on top of a quantised base model, so large models fine-tune on modest hardware.
Direct Preference Optimization — aligns a model directly from preferred/dispreferred answer pairs without a separate reward model.
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback — aligns a model using a reward model trained on human preferences.
A framework of reference-free metrics (faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall) for evaluating RAG systems.
The share of queries whose relevant passage appears in the top k retrieved results.
Mean Reciprocal Rank — averages 1/rank of the first relevant result across queries.
Normalised Discounted Cumulative Gain — a ranking metric that rewards relevant results placed higher.
An attack that smuggles instructions into model input (directly or via retrieved content) to override intended behaviour.
An LLM that plans and calls tools in a loop toward a goal, rather than producing a single fixed response.
A loop pattern interleaving reasoning traces with tool actions and observations.
The token budget available to the model for a single request; everything must fit prompt, evidence and answer.
